scope: Independent bounded five-frame actual full24 late insertion contact/support assessment
actual_findings: By42.015s both physical body panels are already within about1.24-1.27mm of sampled teddy foot/head material. The free rear handle later comes within1.35mm of muzzle material by42.315s.
Held front handle is separated at every inspected actual saved shape by complete tetrahedron/triangle AABB bounds33.52-78.76mm; this does not certify between-frame motion.

The rear handle nearest point changes from material arc96.925mm from its left root at42.315 to394.752mm at42.515-42.795 of424.739mm total (about30mm before right sewn root), still adjacent to muzzle material. This migration is not a topological entanglement proof.

The torso/feet/head and mouth rapidly reconfigure near failure while the rear strap remains close. Aggregate robot reactions alone cannot identify which cloth patch carries which portion of teddy weight.

support_interpretation.evidence: At42.315/42.515 right robot netZ is+1.048/+1.216N, with equal-opposite downward action on coupled soft material. Left robot netZ becomes1.545/1.653N more negative than transport. By failure right netZ is-0.089N and one finger opening reaction collapses, but the preceding rapid shape changes rule out assuming a demonstrated static transfer.

earlier_release_assessment.reason: 42.315/42.515 still have active two-sided grip and downward reaction, yet body and free strap contact and moving mouth are present;42.715 immediately follows a35.15degree reorientation in0.2s. Merely releasing before the opening gate would not prove that the teddy is contained or safely supported.
earlier_release_assessment.bounded_implication: These data support studying load transfer before continued descent, but not selecting an earlier release time from proximity or finger unloading alone. Actual containment is independently reviewed; any future pause/release must preserve existing physical and containment gates.

limitations: Five requested actual frames only, sampled times42.015/42.315/42.515/42.715 and exact failed soft42.795. No first-event claim.
Bear-node/body and handle-sample/bear nearest distances are upper bounds; actual load, friction, penetration-free topology and stable support are not inferred from them.
Body source-face signed normal results are local face sides, not global inside/outside classification.
Exact failed soft frame lacks measured TCP in the NPZ; same-time native guard AIM is separately labeled in source report.
No production edits, threshold changes, new geometry candidates, GPU or native simulation were performed.
